action: NSM advises organisations using Azure API Management to assume all secrets and named values are compromised and rotate all tokens and secrets, check the gateway's RuntimeVersion against NSM's patch thresholds, contact the vendor if not updated, and contact NSM on signs of compromise.
date_note: Day NSM published its notice (updated 23 November); NSM gives no earlier day for the exploitation. The Register reports Microsoft identified the issue on 18 November.
exec: NSM says organisations using Azure API Management should treat stored secrets as compromised; Equinor and Skagerak Energi were among those affected.
impact: NSM says it does not yet know how widely the vulnerability was exploited and has so far no evidence that deliveries at Norwegian organisations were affected.
plain: Norway's security authority says an unknown attacker went after access tokens and other secrets stored in Microsoft's Azure API Management service. Equinor and Skagerak Energi were among those affected. NSM says the flaw should now be closed.

sources.name: NSM (Norwegian National Security Authority): NSM deler tiltak mot sårbarhet i Azure API Management

summary: Norway's National Security Authority (NSM) says an unknown actor actively went after access tokens, secrets and named values in Azure API Management, and names Equinor and Skagerak Energi among affected organisations. NSM says the vulnerability should now be closed but affects several sectors in and beyond Norway. The Register, citing a nonpublic Microsoft advisory, reports Microsoft identified the issue on 18 November, applied a mitigation the next day, and that only Classic tiers were affected.
title: Norway's NSM says an unknown actor went after secrets in Azure API Management; Equinor and Skagerak Energi among affected

validation.note: NSM's own notice read (primary), with The Register (which also saw Microsoft's nonpublic advisory). Skagerak Energi's 18 November release (read, not cited) reports an attempted cyberattack but does not mention APIM; the APIM link is NSM's. No CVE was given on either page.

review.note: stronger than the source: plain said flaw is closed, NSM says it should now be closed; source not about event: removed Skagerak release (no APIM mention). Title, date, severity, Classic tier, actions checked against NSM and The Register.
